NKE.rationale: NKE is a mid-turnaround story with severe fundamental deterioration that has not yet stabilized. Q3 FY2026 diluted EPS of $0.35 is down -35.2% YoY on flat revenue ($11.28B, +0.1% YoY), confirming the problem is margin compression, not volume. Operating margin has collapsed to 5.8% from 7.5% YoY, net margin halved from 9.4% to 4.8%, and operating cash flow cratered -76% YoY to $430M. ROE has compressed from 32.2% to 16.0%. The P/E of 26.9x is actually more expensive than a year ago (20.5x) because earnings fell faster than the stock — the stock is not cheap, it is expensive on deteriorating earnings. The earnings yield of 3.7% sits below the 10Y Treasury at 4.4%, offering a negative equity risk premium. While the Elliott Hill 'Win Now' turnaround is directionally correct (wholesale up 5-8% in recent quarters) and the brand remains strong (Brand Finance BSI 94.7/100), three simultaneous headwinds — tariffs ($1.5B annualized cost, 320 bps gross margin drag), Greater China guided down ~20% in Q4, and accelerating competitive share loss from On (+40%), Hoka (+24%), and a resurgent Adidas — make margin recovery uncertain and distant. The one-time tariff refund (~$1B per Telsey) flatters Q4 EPS but is non-recurring and should not be capitalized. The June 30 earnings report is a critical proof point but the burden of proof is on the company to show margin stabilization and cash flow inflection, neither of which is evidenced yet. P/B at 4.3x (floor of range) provides no margin of safety when ROE is still compressing. The fundamental trajectory is negative, valuation is not cheap on an earnings basis, and the near-term catalyst (Q4 earnings) carries more downside risk (further China deterioration, tariff clarity) than upside given the one-time nature of the refund benefit.
